chunks.sectionTitle: I NTROD u CTION TO E LECTROMA g NETICS
chunks.content:
10.1 I NTROD u CTION TO E LECTROMA g NETICS
Electromagnetics (EM) govern many applications in engineering such as
the transmission lines system. Therefore, it is essential to understand the
fundamental concepts of EM in order to properly design and model electrical
systems and devices using the finite element method (FEM). Furthermore,
EM becomes more useful in designing engineering systems with recent
technologies, especially due to the increasing speeds of digital devices and the
increased use of modern electronics circuits such as printed-circuit-board
and communications systems such as cellular phones. The most important
equations in EM theory are Maxwell’s equations, which are known as the
foundation of EM theory.

chunks.title: finiteelementanalysis_aprimer
chunks.heading: 10.2 M A x WELL ’ S Equ ATIONS AND C ONTIN u ITY
chunks.sectionTitle: M A x WELL ’ S Equ ATIONS AND C ONTIN u ITY
chunks.content:
10.2 M A x WELL ’ S Equ ATIONS AND C ONTIN u ITY
Equ ATION
In electromagnetic analysis on a macroscopic level, it is based on solving the
Maxwell’s equations issue on certain boundary conditions. Also, there is another
fundamental equation that can specify the conservation (indestructibility) of
352 Finite e lement An A lysis
electric charge know as the equation of continuity. Maxwell’s equations and
continuity equation can be written in both differential and integral forms. We
choose to start here with the differential form because it leads to differential
equations that the finite element method (FEM) can handle.
